researcher_notes:
Restaurant365 and Crunchtime both already exist in the graph, so this batch only adds genuinely new brand relationships not already captured. Restaurant365 had 4 existing relationships (Taco John's, Felipe's Mexican Taqueria, BRG Hospitality, Bavarian Bierhaus) -- ran `query-vendor` first per instructions and added 8 new ones from R365's own case-study library (GPS Hospitality/Burger King at ~400 locations across 8 states, Whataburger/GVCS, Carl's Jr./SDC Restaurants, Dave's Hot Chicken/Lion Chaser, Tropical Smoothie Cafe/SERVE Hospitality, Black Rock Coffee Bar [the only brand-corporate, all-locations record in this sub-batch], Jimmy John's/D&D Management, Taziki's Mediterranean Cafe). Nearly every R365 case study is explicitly a single-franchisee deployment, not a brand-corporate decision -- scored vendor_role=franchisee_deployment accordingly except Black Rock Coffee Bar. Crunchtime had 6 distinct existing brands (Five Guys, Chipotle, Jersey Mike's, City Barbeque, Golden Corral, Cotton Patch Cafe, plus a likely-duplicate '54th Street Grill & Bar'/'54th Street Restaurant & Drafthouse' pair already in the graph); this batch adds exactly the Zenput product-line ground flagged as legitimately new: Wingstop (brand-corporate, 2,000+ locations, Ops Summit 2024/April 2025 write-up) and Tacala Companies' 300+-location Taco Bell franchisee rollout (case-study PDF corroborated by search-indexed text; PDF itself was not machine-readable so treated as Medium confidence).

Corporate-structure correction: the task brief's premise that Compeat was 'acquired by PAR Technology in 2019' does not check out against multiple independent sources (PR Newswire, Restaurant Dive, QSR Magazine, Serent Capital) -- Compeat was actually acquired by Restaurant365 itself, announced 2021-06-10/14. No PAR Technology-Compeat transaction was found anywhere. Compeat is now a Restaurant365-owned brand/product line (similar to how xtraCHEF sits inside Toast), which is presumably why almost no Compeat-branded case study activity exists after 2021 -- the only solid dated record found (Taffer's Tavern, 2020-09-01) predates the acquisition. Fourth's history was confirmed as briefed: HotSchedules and Fourth merged July 2019 under Marlin Equity Partners, and the global holding company was renamed Fourth Enterprises, LLC in Nov 2020, with 'HotSchedules' retained as the workforce-management product brand -- not defunct, just a two-tier naming structure. Ottimate's 2023 rename from Plate IQ is confirmed settled and current, no further changes found. xtraCHEF is confirmed to be a wholly-owned Toast product line since Toast's June 2021 acquisition; researched here as its own product per instructions, with only two named restaurant-chain customers found (most xtraCHEF marketing leans on Toast's own POS case-study library instead). Craftable (Bevager/Foodager) remains independent (Gauge Capital-backed, no acquisition found) but evidence came back thin -- only one usable case study. Yellow Dog Inventory (company name: Yellow Dog Software) came back with zero usable restaurant-chain evidence -- its public case studies/testimonials are single-property hotels or ambiguous venues, not multi-unit restaurant brands. Galley Solutions and Ottimate evidence also skews thin/generic (passing mentions in funding-round press coverage or multi-concept operator names rather than dedicated, named-chain case studies).
